views.name: bikeshare_station_reference
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,
  name AS station_name,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  dockcount,
  landmark,
  installation_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_stations`
grain: station_id, one row per bikeshare station
views.description: Normalized station reference: one row per station_id with canonical columns for joins. Use when joining station metadata to trips or status. Preserves spatial coords and installation_date. | Use for: Enrich trips or status with station location or dockcount; Map stations or compute station-level aggregates; Filter stations by landmark or installation_date

views.name: bikeshare_status_time_series
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,
  bikes_available,
  docks_available,
  time AS sample_time,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn_desc_time,
  UNIX_SECONDS(time) AS sample_epoch_seconds,
  SUM(bikes_available) OVER (PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY time
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_bikes_available_total,
  COUNT(1) OVER (PARTITION BY station_id) AS sample_count_per_station
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_status`
grain: station_id + sample_time, one row per status sample
views.description: Time-ordered station status samples with per-station running totals and row_number per station-time. Useful for computing availability trends, last-known status per station, or sampling intervals. | Use for: Get latest status per station by filtering rn_desc_time = 1; Compute moving averages or availability trends per station; Estimate sampling frequency or total samples per station

views.name: bikeshare_trip_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  trip_id,
  duration_sec,
  start_date AS start_timestamp,
  end_date AS end_timestamp,
  start_station_id,
  start_station_name,
  end_station_id,
  end_station_name,
  bike_number,
  NULLIF(TRIM(zip_code), '') AS zip_code,
  subscriber_type
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
grain: trip_id, one row per bikeshare trip
views.description: Cleaned bikeshare trip events: one row per trip with canonical start/end datetimes and durations. Use for trip-level analysis, joins to stations, and subscriber segmentation. | Use for: Trip duration distributions and median/mean durations; Origin-destination flow counts by station; Subscriber type comparisons and home-zip analyses

views.name: sfpd_incident_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,
  category,
  descript,
  dayofweek,
  pddistrict,
  resolution,
  address,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  timestamp AS incident_timestamp,
  pdid
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.sfpd_incidents`
grain: unique_key, one row per police incident
views.description: Police incident events with canonical timestamp and location. One row per incident preserving category and district useful for crime-rate time series or spatial joins. | Use for: Time series of incidents by category or district; Spatial joins to blocks, neighborhoods, or stations; Merge with 311 or SFFD events by time/location proximity

views.name: sffd_service_call_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  row_id,
  call_number,
  unit_id,
  incident_number,
  call_type,
  call_date,
  received_timestamp,
  dispatch_timestamp,
  response_timestamp,
  on_scene_timestamp,
  transport_timestamp,
  hospital_timestamp,
  available_timestamp,
  call_final_disposition,
  address,
  city,
  zipcode_of_incident,
  battalion,
  station_area,
  final_priority,
  als_unit,
  call_type_group,
  number_of_alarms,
  unit_type,
  unit_sequence_in_call_dispatch,
  supervisor_district,
  neighborhood_district,
  latitude,
  longitude
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.sffd_service_calls`
grain: row_id, one row per call-unit dispatched
views.description: Fire/EMS service calls normalized: one row per call-unit (row_id) preserving timestamps for lifecycle analysis and spatial columns for mapping and joins. | Use for: Analyze response times between dispatch and on_scene; Count calls by call_type_group or station_area; Map EMS transports and hospitals visited

views.name: trees_point_locations
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  tree_id,
  legal_status,
  species,
  address,
  site_order,
  site_info,
  plant_type,
  care_taker,
  care_assistant,
  plant_date,
  dbh,
  plot_size,
  permit_notes,
  x_coordinate,
  y_coordinate,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  location
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.street_trees`
grain: tree_id, one row per street tree
views.description: Street trees table projected to one row per tree with spatial coordinates and species. Use for species counts, spatial joins, or planting-date analysis. | Use for: Species distribution and counts by neighborhood; Find trees within spatial radius of a point or station; Analyze planting trends over time

views.name: service_requests_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,
  created_date,
  closed_date,
  resolution_action_updated_date,
  status,
  status_notes,
  agency_name,
  category,
  complaint_type,
  descriptor,
  incident_address,
  supervisor_district,
  neighborhood,
  source,
  media_url,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  police_district
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.311_service_requests`
grain: unique_key, one row per 311 service request
views.description: 311 service requests normalized: one row per request with created/closed timestamps, status, category and spatial columns for temporal or spatial analysis. | Use for: Time-to-close analyses and backlog counts by agency; Spatial clustering of complaint categories; Cross-compare 311 requests with SFPD or SFFD events by time/location

views.name: station_daily_trip_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  start_station_id,
  DATE(start_date) AS trip_date,
  COUNT(1) AS trips_start_count,
  AVG(duration_sec) AS avg_duration_sec,
  SUM(CASE WHEN subscriber_type IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS trips_with_subscriber_info
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
GROUP BY start_station_id, DATE(start_date)
grain: start_station_id + trip_date, one row per station per day
views.description: Daily aggregated trips per station (as origin): counts and average duration per day per start_station_id. Use for time-series station activity and trend detection. | Use for: Daily activity trends per station; Detect seasonality or weekday patterns in trips; Compare average trip durations across stations

views.name: station_latest_status_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,
  bikes_available,
  docks_available,
  time AS sample_time,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn_desc_time
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_status`
grain: station_id + sample_time, one row per status sample (ranked per station)
views.description: Latest known status per station using ranking by time. Expose rn_desc_time so consumers can filter to the most recent sample (rn_desc_time = 1). Useful for real-time dashboarding or availability snapshots. | Use for: Select most recent availability per station by filtering rn_desc_time = 1; Show top-N stations by available bikes at latest sample using rn_desc_time = 1 then rank

views.name: incidents_weekly_counts_by_category
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  category,
  pddistrict,
  EXTRACT(ISOWEEK FROM CAST(timestamp AS DATE)) AS iso_week,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(timestamp AS DATE)) AS year,
  COUNT(1) AS incident_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.sfpd_incidents`
GROUP BY category, pddistrict, year, iso_week
grain: category + pddistrict + year + iso_week, one row per category-district-week
views.description: Weekly counts of SFPD incidents by category and police district. Use for trend analysis and seasonal comparison at week granularity. | Use for: Week-over-week incident trends by category or district; Seasonal comparisons across years for a category
